lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The date of birth should be removed.
items.because: It does not help establish product-role fit and can introduce unnecessary bias or screening concerns.

items.says: The nationality should be removed.
items.because: It does not help establish product-role fit and can introduce unnecessary bias or screening concerns.

items.says: The résumé lacks a product-focused headline or summary.
items.because: A recruiter should not have to infer the target role from the sections below.

items.says: The MBA completion date should reflect the applicant’s actual status when applying.
The economics degree could be visually secondary to the MBA.
items.because: The MBA better supports the current product positioning.

items.says: Harbor Payments should appear before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The internship ended in 2024, after the Crestline role ended in 2023, and reverse-chronological order is expected.

items.says: The late-delivery reduction may reflect a changed calculation rather than better delivery performance.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can improve the reported rate without making deliveries more reliable.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% pick-error reduction is relative or a percentage-point change.
Make the two-site scope and retraining details easier to parse.
items.because: The bullet packs the result, intervention, rollout, and training into a lot of information.

items.says: Explain how the forecast-error comparison was measured.
Clarify whether the annual driver-hour savings were measured or projected.
items.because: Those imply different levels of demonstrated impact.

items.says: Give the baseline, measurement period, and meaning of the 35% conversion improvement.
items.because: Readers need to know whether it is a relative lift or a percentage-point increase.

items.says: Clarify the evidence attributing the conversion improvement to the new flow.
items.because: A result this significant needs substantiation.

items.says: Clarify the rollout and measurement scope behind “for all merchants.”
items.because: The phrase invites questions about which merchants were included.

items.says: Add a verified customer or business outcome for dispute self-service if available.
items.because: Shipping early does not establish what the feature achieved.

items.says: Specify the currency for “1.1 million dollars.”
Clarify whether the chargeback-loss figure is observed, estimated, or annualized.
Use US spelling consistently instead of “analysed.”
items.because: The résumé mixes spelling forms with US contact and location details.

items.says: Consider giving ticket triage less space unless it demonstrates meaningful ownership.
items.because: It reads more like operational support than product management.

items.says: Do not treat the opt-in comparison as causal evidence without a supporting design.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not, creating selection bias.

items.says: Explain how the opt-in analysis relates to the following onboarding result.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: Explain how median time to first payment was measured and whether the pilot had a suitable baseline.
Lead the Harbor Payments entry with its strongest product outcome and discovery evidence.
items.because: A lower-level operational task should not compete for early attention.

items.says: Clarify the measurement basis for the food tonnage.
Ensure “first year” matches the project dates.
Use US spelling consistently instead of “tonnes.”
items.because: The résumé mixes spelling forms with US contact and location details.

items.says: Keep the implied link between reminders and user growth proportionate.
items.because: The interviews informed the change, but weekly active users may have grown for other reasons.

items.says: State the user-growth measurement period consistently.
Clarify whether staff cover shifts were measured over comparable periods.
Avoid repeating the dining-hall partnership detail without adding value.
items.because: It may overlap with the first project bullet.

items.says: Add a concrete outcome for the weekly working sessions if one can be substantiated.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity rather than what changed.

items.says: Make your role in the patient-intake work clear.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your contribution.

items.says: Clarify the practical effect of the shorter intake form, if known.
items.because: The result is vague.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result does not belong under the hospital practicum as written.
items.because: It describes merchant payments and appears copied from the Harbor Payments experience.

items.says: Support the A/B testing skill with controlled-experiment experience or remove it.
items.because: The opt-in comparison is not necessarily an A/B test.

items.says: Show more depth in the tools section, adding tools only if they can be discussed competently.
items.because: The section is short and does not show depth.
